title: [BUG] npm 12.2.2 bundles glob and minimatch versions affected by October 2026 advisories
body:
### Problem

The registry `latest` release, npm 12.2.2 (published November 4, 2026), still bundles `glob@13.0.6` and `minimatch@10.2.5`. Both match public reviewed advisory ranges:

- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 — glob cancellation can leave filesystem traversal running; patched in 14.0.2.
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 — minimatch pattern preprocessing can amplify CPU/memory use; patched in 11.0.1 (current latest 11.0.8).

This is a dependency inventory/audit reproduction, not a claim that every npm command exposes an exploitable path. No resource-exhaustion payload is necessary to reproduce the audit result.

### Minimal reproduction

With supported Node.js (tested on Node 26), create this package.json in an empty directory:

```json
{
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": { "npm": "12.2.2" },
  "overrides": { "glob": "14.0.2", "minimatch": "11.0.8" }
}
```

Run `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`, then `npm audit --package-lock-only --json --audit-level=low` (the metadata-only reproduction uses npm 11.20.0 to inspect the npm 12.2.2 package). Inspect the lockfile entries `node_modules/npm/node_modules/glob` and `node_modules/npm/node_modules/minimatch`: they remain 13.0.6 and 10.2.5 despite the consumer overrides. The audit identifies the two advisories and propagates them through npm's internal parents (21 moderate package findings, not 21 independent vulnerabilities).

The same two bundled versions are present in the published npm tarball. An application's ordinary audit does not cover a separately installed global npm CLI, so an otherwise clean application audit cannot establish that the package-manager tool is clean.

### Expected / suggested change

Please migrate npm's internal glob/minimatch consumers to compatible patched versions, regenerate the bundled dependency tree, and publish a new CLI release. Updating the top-level declarations alone will not replace nested bundled copies. Validate install, ci, pack, and publish dry-run behavior with the refreshed bundle; preserve supported Node patch floors. If a supported consumer repair procedure exists for bundled npm dependencies, documenting it would also help.

### Local handling

In https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n/pull/44 we retain the latest official npm CLI for its CI/release behavior and keep it outside the application dependency lock. We tried consumer overrides as above; they do not repair the bundle. We have not replaced incompatible npm internals in place or downgraded to the old npm version proposed by audit. The requirement that all tooling have no unresolved advisories remains explicitly unfinished pending a supported upstream fix.

Related issue searches for the two exact advisory IDs returned no results on November 13, 2026. Older minimatch/brace-expansion reports concern different advisory IDs.
